Bounded cluster search for addition commutativity

OutcomeFour GCTS searches13-line ordinary candidate152 primitive commandsComplete costsExact evidence

All four bounded GCTS searches remain unknown. Their complete independently reconstructed traces now pass. A separate ordinary forward-chaining control automatically produced a 13-line candidate, but this exceeds the frozen 12-row comparison. Its complete whole-native workspace estimate exceeds the fixed boundary, so no whole native target query was executed and commutativity remains native-unknown.

The exact target is \(\forall\,\mathit{x}\;\left(\forall\,\mathit{y}\;\left(\left(\mathit{x}+\mathit{y}\right)=\left(\mathit{y}+\mathit{x}\right)\right)\right)\). The original theory contains \(\forall\,\mathit{x}\;\left(\left(\mathit{x}+0\right)=\mathit{x}\right)\) and \(\forall\,\mathit{x}\;\left(\forall\,\mathit{y}\;\left(\left(\mathit{x}+\operatorname{S}\!\left(\mathit{y}\right)\right)=\operatorname{S}\!\left(\left(\mathit{x}+\mathit{y}\right)\right)\right)\right)\), with the same enabled natural-number induction scheme.

GCTS result

Two base runs reached 5,000 attempts; two fixed cluster runs reached the 60-second cap. No proof was found. All 15,679 nodes and 589 policy events/hints were independently replayed.

Ordinary result

The full 153-hyperedge closure produced 13 lines in 0.099 seconds internally measured before final artifact serialization. This is an ordinary discovery, with whole host/tree cross-checks, and a native workspace unknown. It is not a GCTS or RL discovery.

This is useful negative evidence about the present ordering and proposal cost. The 13-line ordinary upper bound does not establish that a 12-line proof is impossible. No speed advantage, full Peano arithmetic completeness or RL training claim follows.

Same language and complete base fallback

All four fresh models retain 17,158 placements, 48 initially active required points and 12 proof rows. The same complete five-node contextual grammar exposes both induction variables, all declared quantifier closures, every expression occurrence/direction/substitution and every strict-prior source binding. The preserved formula-ID dictionary has 2,069 entries; 96 formulas are active outputs or premises.

Fixed runs reached the wall ceiling after 2,832 and 2,843 attempts; the final sampler overshoots of 0.030549 and 0.154488 seconds are preserved as search-budget unknowns. These mixed caps do not establish equal work. The fixed policy spent about 44 seconds per run on proposals; complete serialization cost another 85–148 seconds per observation.

The fixed proposer uses authored weights over a bounded pool of validated continuation clusters, including open arbitrary shapes. Forty-two parameterized families backed by the two actual discovered lemmas expose 13,860 internally compatible bindings. Proposal membership only reorders original incident candidates; global dead checks, forced propagation, earliest-generation branching, every remaining base fallback and exact failed-child rollback are preserved. The 94 generic local interfaces are authored infrastructure, not learned lemmas. No compatible policy was trained and these fixed scores are not RL.

The full independent auditor reconstructed all candidate point data and every recorded graph census, decision, proposal pool, work count, feature, fixed score, continuation, fallback and rollback. The small preflight fixtures alone did not exercise failed-child backtracking; the actual target traces supply that evidence.
